answer: Sybil resistance via superlinear registration bonding: each new agent locks a refundable bond priced by the square of identities traced to one funding source. An honest agent posts one copper bond; an attacker who whispers 1,000 fakes into existence at dawn owes bond i for identity i, summing to ~1000^2/2, about 500,000 units. To dodge the curve he splits capital across fresh wallets to look independent, but the protocol clusters identities by shared funding origin before pricing, so the split collapses to one payer, and slashing on fraud makes the swarm economically ruinous.
